issues.description: Re-ingest clears warnings/stats but not results, so deleted input files leave stale rows in the database.
Ingest is not atomic because each row is committed separately, leaving partial database updates after a later parse failure.
Harness B JSONL assumes every decoded value is an object; arrays or strings crash with AttributeError.
Malformed Harness C XML is not caught, so one bad XML file crashes the entire ingest.
XML parsing uses xml.etree directly on input files without hardening or size limits, exposing the CLI to XML denial-of-service inputs.
NaN scores are accepted by parse_score and then crash SQLite insertion with a NOT NULL constraint failure.
Required fields like run_id, model, and task are not validated, allowing blank IDs and silent duplicate overwrites.
Harness A reads the CSV header but never validates it, so reordered or missing columns are silently misinterpreted.
Invalid JSON and invalid numeric scores are reported as missing_score, making data-quality reporting misleading.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the user-supplied target directory without guardrails.
Tests cover the planted fixture path but miss malformed JSONL, malformed XML, stale-row reingest, blank IDs, and NaN scores.
